headline: High: Notion AI can exfiltrate workspace content to vendor backends, while the paired awesome-nlp profile is too underspecified to rule out unsafe downstream use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between awesome-nlp and Notion AI, so prompt injection is not default. However, Notion AI ingests workspace pages and can be influenced by page content, while awesome-nlp is an unverified open-source NLP list with no I/O surfaces described. The pairwise bridge is therefore possible only through manual content transfer or undocumented orchestration.
conditions: IF a user copies awesome-nlp-derived text into a Notion page that Notion AI reads, injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator feeds awesome-nlp output into Notion AI without sanitization, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Require manual review before pasting generated text into Notion.
Strip instructions from imported text before Notion AI reads it.
Use a fixed template for any handoff content.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content and calls vendor backends; awesome-nlp has no documented data handling, so the pair can leak workspace content if outputs are copied into the open-source side or if Notion AI summarizes sensitive pages. The interaction is not proven, but the default Notion side is enough to create a realistic leakage path.
conditions: IF sensitive workspace pages are processed by Notion AI, those contents may be sent to vendor backends.
IF Notion AI output is exported into any downstream system built around awesome-nlp, sensitive text can propagate further.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in Notion pages used with AI.
Restrict Notion AI to non-sensitive workspaces.
Review and redact pages before AI summarization.
Disable any downstream export from Notion AI outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on workspace content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp exposes no write or network capabilities in its profile, while Notion AI has vendor-hosted workspace actions but no filesystem write or git modification. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is limited. Uncertainty remains because awesome-nlp is unverified and its runtime surface is not described.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp is wrapped in an external tool that writes to the same workspace as Notion AI, conflicts can emerge.
IF an orchestrator grants awesome-nlp write access not shown in the profile, overlap may occur.
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp read-only.
Do not grant shared write access to the same directory.
Run Notion AI only on its native workspace data.
Check orchestrator permissions before pairing.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so if awesome-nlp output is pasted into Notion, Notion may treat it as authoritative content. The pair lacks a verification step, and Notion can then summarize or act on flawed text. Because the bridge is manual or orchestrated rather than default, medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF awesome-nlp output is copied into a Notion page used for Q&A, Notion AI may propagate errors.
IF a workflow treats Notion AI summaries as final without human review, cascading errors can spread.
mitigations: Require human review of any imported text.
Mark imported content as untrusted.
Use source links in Notion pages.
Compare summaries against original sources.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends content to vendor backends, while awesome-nlp is open-source and unverified with no residency or retention controls documented. If regulated workspace data is processed in Notion, compliance obligations may differ from any local use of awesome-nlp. The other agent is not cited for a specific residency rule because none is documented.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated content is entered into Notion AI without an approved DPA, residency/compliance risk increases.
IF retention or deletion requirements apply to workspace pages, Notion AI processing may conflict with them.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI workflows.
Confirm DPA and residency terms before use.
Limit AI access to non-regulated workspaces.
Document retention and deletion handling.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing.
